mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact corporate earnings and drive up stock prices, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time over the next 20 days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate suggests easier monetary policy, which can stimulate borrowing and investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases by 0.25% in the last month
failure_condition: If the federal funds rate decreases but S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05), this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment suggests a strong labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and higher corporate revenues, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If payroll employment increases but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 35% of the time, this hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates higher economic activity, which can lead to increased demand for goods and services, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases but S&P 500 returns are not positive in more than 60% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts indicates reduced demand in the housing market, which can lead to decreased economic activity and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts decrease but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A high and rising CPI suggests inflationary pressures, which may lead to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If CPI increases but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 35% of the time, this hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of increasing payroll employment and decreasing unemployment rate suggests a strong labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and higher corporate revenues, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If both payroll employment increases and unemployment decreases but S&P 500 returns are not positive in more than 60% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high federal funds rate and increasing CPI suggests tight monetary conditions with inflationary pressures, which can lead to decreased corporate profitability and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 35% of the time, this hypothesis fails.
